name: altered level of consciousness overview
title: Altered level of consciousness: treat the reversible causes first, then the exam (brainstem reflexes, each with its in and out pathway, breathing, motor response, eye opening and signs of awareness, scored in coma by the GCS or FOUR score) places the patient as brain death, coma, vegetative state, minimally conscious state minus or plus, or a locked-in coma mimic

root.title: Not responding: FIRST look for the TREATABLE causes
lines: shock or low blood pressure · low glucose · diabetic ketoacidosis · hypertensive encephalopathy · drug intoxication
bacterial or fungal meningitis · herpes simplex encephalitis · brain abscess · epidural or subdural hematoma
also consider: syncope · seizure, post-ictal state · encephalopathy, delirium
then EXAMINE: is the patient AWAKE (alertness = VOLUME) and AWARE (awareness = TUNING, the cortex)?
alertness: ascending reticular activating system, upper pons + midbrain → thalamus, hypothalamus → cortex

groups.title: NOT aware
lines: brainstem reflexes and eye opening decide

pres.title: Brainstem reflexes: in → out
lines: • pupil: II → III (Edinger-Westphal) · blown pupil = uncal herniation
• Horner: ptosis, miosis ± anhidrosis · 3-neuron sympathetic path
• doll's eyes (no C-spine concern) + calorics: VIII → III, IV, VI
• calorics in COMA: only SLOW deviation toward cold · COWS is the awake fast phase
• corneal: V → VII · gag: IX → X · cough: often the LAST lost

head: h
Brain death
Canadian criteria: ALL of
awake: • known cause that can cause it
exam: • deep coma, no motor response (spinal reflexes allowed)
• NO pupil (mid-size or larger), corneal, vestibulo-ocular, gag, cough

head: h
Coma
both hemispheres, both thalami, or brainstem above the mid-pons
awake: case: 79 y, 36 h headache, stiff neck, 39.5 °C · antibiotics · intubated within 12 h
case: 67 y cardiac arrest, ~15 min to rhythm · day 2 extends right arm to pain
exam: • decorticate: arms FLEX, legs extend → above the red nucleus
• decerebrate: all EXTEND → below the red nucleus
• triple flexion (hip, knee, ankle): SPINAL, no brainstem needed

head: h
Vegetative state
aka UNRESPONSIVE WAKEFULNESS syndrome
exam: • grimace, yawn, roving eyes, flexion withdrawal
• sounds but no words, no commands
case: 26 y, head injury, 2 years on · eyes open, yawns, sleep-wake cycles

head: h
Locked-in syndrome
NOT a disorder of consciousness
eeg: other mimics: Guillain-Barré, myasthenia, neuromuscular blockade, akinetic mutism, psychogenic
